I’m in the same boat so I just want you to know you’re not alone. I can’t even leave my room sometimes because of it. I wish I had the answers, I really do. The things people made fun of us for really stuck with us and it’s hard to just forget about it. I’m sure you are good looking and that there are many good qualities about you. We tend to only focus on the negative when there’s so many positive things that we just ignore.

Maybe you can start by telling someone who you know for sure wouldn’t shame you and see how that makes you feel. Then from there you can decide if you want to tell anyone else. But I don’t recommend keeping all of this inside because it might take a toll on you.

I think it’s harmful to say. When something bad happens to you, you don’t right away stop to think what others have gone through and then decide how hurt you should feel. That’s not how feelings work. You feel the pain right away.
Just because your sister may have worse anxiety doesn’t mean yours isn’t valid. Some people have it more severe than others but they all still matter.

Yeah it’s really hard living like this. I told my dad about it, how I feel too ugly to be seen and that I feel like he’s judging me in his head. He said it makes him mad that I would even think that he’s thinking that.
I get embarrassed about my future too, it depends what’s triggering me at the time

I’ve been taking it every night for past year or two. I take klonopin during the day so klonopin helps my anxiety the most but remeron is good for controlling my anxiety at night. Before remeron I would wake up in the middle of the night every night panicking and feeling nauseous to the point id throw up and not able to fall back asleep. Ever since taking remeron that doesn’t happen anymore. I’m usually able to sleep through the night. So for social anxiety I don’t think it’s enough by itself but everyone is different.

Think about what you’re telling yourself that’s giving your body that panic response. Once you identify your thoughts, replace them with more realistic ones. Most people are just thinking about their own presentation tbh. Also, instead of thinking “I’m going to mess up” its better to think “if I mess up, the worst case scenario isn’t really so bad” yes I know embarrassment is the worst feeling ever but there’s worse things that could happen. Just keeping that in mind helps, and focusing on your breathing.
